description: Figure 6(a) illustrates the distribution of datasets over time for the five most frequent researcher locations—the US, India (IN), the UK, Germany (DE), and Canada—combined with all other locations. The horizontal axis represents the year, labeled from 2012 to 2022 in sequential order, with a logarithmic scale. The vertical axis represents the number of datasets, labeled “Number of datasets,” with a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ to 10⁴, and tick labels are regularly spaced at intervals of 10⁰, 10¹, 10², 10³, and 10⁴. Five bars represent the five most frequent researcher locations, each with a distinct color: blue for the US, orange for India, green for the UK, red for Germany, and light blue for Canada. Additionally, a gray bar represents all other locations combined. The US bar consistently shows the highest number of datasets across all years, starting at approximately 10¹ in 2012 and reaching approximately 10³ in 2022. India’s bar begins at approximately 10⁰ in 2012, rises to approximately 10² in 2017, and then decreases to approximately 10¹ in 2022. The UK bar starts at approximately 10⁰ in 2012, peaks at approximately 10² in 2016, and then declines to approximately 10¹ in 2022. Germany’s bar begins at approximately 10⁰ in 2012, rises to approximately 10¹ in 2017, and then decreases to approximately 10⁰ in 2022. Canada’s bar remains relatively low throughout the period, starting at approximately 10⁰ in 2012 and reaching approximately 10¹ in 2022. The “Other” locations bar fluctuates between approximately 10⁰ and 10¹ throughout the years. The bars are arranged chronologically by year, and no bars are visually emphasized with shading, bolding, outlining, or annotations.
